title: AI customer feedback triage with Airtable, Slack and Gmail
metaTitle: AI customer feedback triage agent | Pixel2Tech
metaDescription: An n8n agent that classifies form feedback as compliment, complaint or feature request, logs it in Airtable and alerts Slack or replies via Gmail.
summary: An n8n workflow that reads every feedback form submission, classifies it as a compliment, complaint or feature request, files it in the right Airtable table and notifies the right channel.
overview: We built this workflow for a product business that collects customer feedback through a web form. An AI agent on Azure OpenAI reads each submission and decides what kind of feedback it is. The workflow then stores it in a matching Airtable table, posts compliments and feature requests to Slack, and sends complaints an email reply through Gmail.
challenge: Feedback forms fill up with a mix of praise, complaints and ideas. Someone has to read each entry, decide who should see it and log it somewhere useful, and unhappy customers can wait days for a response.
approach: An n8n form trigger captures the customer's name, email and message. An AI agent running on an Azure OpenAI chat model classifies the feedback. A merge step joins the classification with the original form data, and a Switch node routes it by type. Each branch creates a record in its own Airtable table for compliments, complaints or feature requests. Compliments and feature requests are posted to Slack for the team, while complaints trigger a Gmail message back to the customer.
outcome: Every piece of feedback is now sorted and filed as it arrives, the team sees praise and ideas in Slack, and customers with a complaint get an email response straight away.

process.title: Set up storage
process.body: We built an Airtable base with separate tables for compliments, complaints and feature requests.

process.title: Classify and route
process.body: We configured the Azure OpenAI agent and a Switch node to send each entry down the right branch.

process.title: Notify and test
process.body: We connected Slack and Gmail, then tested each branch with sample feedback.

whyItMatters: Fast replies to complaints and a clean record of feature requests both depend on sorting feedback the moment it arrives.

faqs.q: Can it pull feedback from email or reviews instead of a form?
faqs.a: Yes. The trigger can be swapped for an inbox, a review platform or a helpdesk, and the classification and routing stay the same.

faqs.a: Yes. We adapt the workflow to your tools and process, including your own feedback categories, and give you a fixed quote after a short call.
